edges.dependent: Home Access: DSL, Cable, and FTTH
edges.rationale: Home access technologies are defined as the means by which a residential end system connects to the network; understanding what an end system is and its role is needed before studying how it gains access.
Ethernet and WiFi access describe how end systems (hosts) attach to LANs and hotspots, so the concept of an end system must come first.
Cellular access is framed as untethered connectivity for hand-held end systems; the end-system concept underpins why this access type exists.

edges.dependent: Home Access: DSL, Cable, and FTTH
edges.rationale: DSL runs over twisted-pair telephone lines, cable over coaxial HFC, and FTTH over optical fiber; understanding these media's properties is needed to grasp how each access technology works and its data rates.
The wired Ethernet portion of this topic depends on knowing twisted-pair (and fiber) characteristics; the dependency applies to the Ethernet half, not WiFi.
The WiFi (802.11) portion operates over radio channels; understanding wireless propagation and radio bands is needed to understand wireless LAN access.
Cellular access (3G/LTE/5G) fundamentally relies on radio transmission over licensed spectrum and propagation behavior, so unguided media concepts are a direct prerequisite.
